findings.finding: The plan assumes init_core is the only caller of init._git that needs a GitTimedOut catch. It is not. pending_init_is_symlink, pending_init_attaches_to_existing and pending_init_remote_unreachable all call init._git (through _git_ok and _main_worktree_tracker) outside init_core. The strict auto-init path _cli/_init.py::_create_tracker (via ensure_initialized) calls them before init_core and has no exception handler. After step 2, a stalled git in that pre-check would surface as an uncaught GitTimedOut traceback instead of the planned 'Error: … timed out; rebar init stopped' message and exit 1.
scenarios: A linked worktree under the same host stall runs any CLI arm that needs a store. ensure_initialized -> _create_tracker -> pending_init_is_symlink -> _main_worktree_tracker -> init._git times out -> GitTimedOut escapes as a Python traceback.

Option 2: catch GitTimedOut in _create_tracker, write the same 'Error: <cmd> timed out after 120s; rebar init stopped' line, and raise SystemExit(1). findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure-disposition statement per arm (init timeout, sweep stop, write failure in gc-config/merge-ours): transient/retryable vs fatal, the exit code and token surfaced, and the recovery (re-run init, next sweep), including MCP-boot and fsck --repair behaviour.

No disposition word (retryable/transient/fatal) or rebar retry token (e.g. exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY) appears for the timeout arm.
findings.finding: The plan changes how a watchdog timeout surfaces (a new GitTimedOut exception, a sweep stop, init exit 1) but never states its disposition: transient/retryable versus fatal. The root cause is a host-load stall that passed on rerun, i.e. transient. Yet init surfaces it as a generic 'exit 1' with 'rebar init stopped', indistinguishable from a permanent init error. Two things are also unstated: whether re-running init after a partial init is safe and is the intended recovery, and what the MCP-boot and fsck --repair callers see or do when the sweep reports a stopped unit.
scenarios: An automation or agent sees exit 1 from rebar init on a loaded host, treats it as fatal, and does not retry, although a rerun would succeed.
MCP boot's sweep stops at gc-config. Whether the server boots degraded, logs or errors is unstated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' paragraph with three arms. (1) GitTimedOut in init is transient: state the exit code (consider rebar's retryable exit/WAIT_AND_RETRY convention instead of a bare 1) and that re-running init is idempotent. (2) A sweep stop is transient: the units are retried on the next sweep, and MCP boot and fsck --repair log the failed unit and continue. (3) A config write failure (config.lock) is transient: recorded failed and retried on the next sweep.

findings.finding: The plan adds a new public `GitTimedOut(RuntimeError)` plus `stop_on_git_timeout` in `rebar._store.ensures`. The codebase already has the same construct: a private `_SyncGitTimedOut(Exception)` that stores the timed-out `operation`, and a `_git` closure that raises it when `git_outcome.is_watchdog_timeout(cp)` is true. The plan does not mention it, so after this change there would be two parallel 'git watchdog timed out, stop now' exceptions. Promoting the existing one would give three call sites (fsck sync check, init._git, _init_ensures._git), which meets Rule of Three for a shared helper. Leaving two copies invites drift: different attribute names, base classes and message formats.
scenarios: A later change to how a timed-out command is named (e.g. `args[:2]` vs the full argv) is made in one exception but not the other, so fsck WARN text and init error text disagree.
A future caller has to choose between two equivalent exceptions, one of them private to an fsck module.
findings.suggested_fix: Define `GitTimedOut(RuntimeError)` with an `operation` attribute and `stop_on_git_timeout(result, *args)` once, either in `rebar._store.git_outcome` next to `is_watchdog_timeout` or in ensures.py as the plan proposes. Replace `_SyncGitTimedOut` in fsck_tracker_health.py with it (its `_git` closure then becomes `return stop_on_git_timeout(run_git_bounded(...), *args)`). Add fsck_tracker_health.py to Scope and run the existing fsck sync-status tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State recovery for a watchdog-killed git that leaves `.git/config.lock` behind (detection, or an operator message naming the lock), and add a test that re-running `rebar init` after a timeout exit converges to a fully-initialised store.
evidence: Findings: 'a git shim that stalls every git config ... before git runs'
Approach 4: return 'failed' ... 'for example a held config.lock'
Testing: 'Recovery: after removing the stub, a second run_ensures returns no failed outcome'
findings.finding: Recovery after a watchdog kill is unaddressed. If a real filesystem stall kills git mid-write (after git created `.git/config.lock`), the stale lock remains. Step 4 then turns every later config write into a permanent `failed` ('could not lock config file'), and the next sweep cannot converge. Likewise, init exiting 1 midway leaves a partly-initialised store, and the plan does not state that re-running `rebar init` converges. The recovery test only removes the stub; the shim stalls before git runs, so it never creates a lock.
scenarios: A stall during git's write is killed by the watchdog and `config.lock` is orphaned; every later sweep reports gc-config/merge-ours failed indefinitely.
`rebar init` exits 1 after `_ensure_branch_user_config` times out; the user re-runs init on a half-built store.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the init_core timeout message from the watchdog result's stderr (or `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`), not a hard-coded '120s'.
evidence: Plan: 'writes `Error: <git command> timed out after 120s; rebar init stopped` to stderr'
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:375: `return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 124, "", f"git timed out after {timeout}s")`

findings.finding: Approach step 5 hard-codes the bound in the user-facing message (`Error: <git command> timed out after 120s; rebar init stopped`). That text is already available: the watchdog result's stderr is built as `git timed out after {timeout}s` (gitutil.py:375), and the bound lives in `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT = 120` (gitutil.py:452). A literal '120s' copies a constant the codebase already owns, and the message would be wrong if the bound or a caller's timeout ever changes.
scenarios: A later change to `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, or a seam that passes a different `timeout=`, leaves init printing a wrong '120s'.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `GitTimedOut` carry the watchdog result's stderr (or the timeout value) and format the message as `Error: git <operation>: <stderr>; rebar init stopped`. Alternatively interpolate `gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, as fsck does with `_FSCK_GIT_TIMEOUT`.

findings.finding: Raising GitTimedOut partway through a fresh init leaves a mounted tracker with an unborn branch. The next `rebar init` takes the 'already initialized' path and never finishes the bootstrap. The plan's own reproduction stalled in `_ensure_branch_user_config`, which runs right after `git worktree add --orphan` and before `commit.gpgsign false`, the initial empty commit, `_commit_precommit` and `_gen_local_files`. After the fix, init exits 1 at that point. On re-run, init_core sees `.tickets-tracker/.git`, `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` succeeds on the unborn branch, and it runs only the ensure sweep, then prints 'Ticket system already initialized.' and returns 0. The tracker user config, gpgsign settings, initial commit and .pre-commit-config.yaml (not an ensure unit) are never applied.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (init_core wrapper) / src/rebar/_commands/init.py init_core lines 150-178 and 200-213, _mount_or_create_branch lines 360-380
scenarios: Partial host stall during a fresh `rebar init`: the user.email check times out, init exits 1, the user re-runs init and gets exit 0 with a store that has no initial commit and no tracker user identity.
The stall starts after `worktree add` in the local or remote branch arm: the worktree is mounted, the post-mount bootstrap is skipped, and the next run reports converged.
findings.suggested_fix: In the init_core wrapper (or a try/except around the post-`_mount_or_create_branch` bootstrap in `_init_core`), when GitTimedOut fires after `_mount_or_create_branch` returned 0 on a branch this run created, undo the mount with the same steps as the 'Clean up a partial/stale tracker dir' block (`git worktree prune` + `_rmtree(tracker)`). The next init then starts fresh. Test: stub `init._git` to time out on `config user.email`, assert exit 1 and that no tracker dir is left, then confirm a second init with the stub removed completes the bootstrap.
